Assemble a correlation matrix from pairwise binary counts

Source: R/suffstat.R
cd_correlation_from_counts.Rd

Builds a positive-definite correlation matrix over a set of binary variables from their pairwise two-by-two co-occurrence counts – the aggregated form in which co-occurrence data (comorbidity, market-basket, species co-occurrence) is usually published. The result feeds straight into cd_discover_suffstat().

Usage

cd_correlation_from_counts(pairs, type = c("phi", "tetra"), repair = TRUE)

Arguments

pairs

A data frame with one row per variable pair and columns var_i, var_j (the two variable identifiers) and n11, n10, n01, n00 (the counts of: both present, the first only, the second only, both absent).

type

"phi" (default; the Pearson correlation of the two indicators, base R) or "tetra" (the latent-Gaussian tetrachoric correlation, which needs the psych package).

repair

Whether to project an indefinite matrix to the nearest positive-definite correlation matrix. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

A correlation matrix with a "repair" attribute recording the minimum eigenvalue before and after repair, the Frobenius distortion, and the pair and variable counts.

Details

A matrix assembled pair by pair is not guaranteed positive semi-definite, so it is repaired to the nearest positive-definite correlation matrix by eigenvalue clipping when repair = TRUE; the eigenvalue floor reached and the repair distortion are recorded in the result's "repair" attribute.

Every unordered variable pair must appear exactly once; a repeated pair is an error rather than a silent overwrite. A pair that is absent from pairs is taken to have zero correlation (the off-diagonal entry stays zero before repair).

See also

cd_discover_suffstat()

Examples

pairs <- data.frame(
  var_i = "a", var_j = "b",
  n11 = 900, n10 = 100, n01 = 100, n00 = 8900)
cd_correlation_from_counts(pairs)
#>           a         b
#> a 1.0000000 0.8888889
#> b 0.8888889 1.0000000
#> attr(,"repair")
#> attr(,"repair")$eig_min_raw
#> [1] 0.1111111
#> 
#> attr(,"repair")$eig_min
#> [1] 0.1111111
#> 
#> attr(,"repair")$distortion
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> attr(,"repair")$n_pairs
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> attr(,"repair")$n_vars
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> attr(,"repair")$type
#> [1] "phi"
#>
